verification_report.summary: Both proposed internal deductions pass strict sequential verification. For positive lower mass, the general minimal-reference theorem gives a finite envelope-class equation. Its finite solution can be compared against every genuine global subsolution through the finite-first-potential relative domination corollary, so its scalar is exactly b_h(f); the greatest exponential solutions enter the same envelope class by one-way upward stability, and a fixed finite non-pluripolar dominator lets the relative continuity theorem upgrade every stated L1-convergent normalized subsequence to capacity convergence and the exact equation. For the nef divisor result, the separately audited threshold-divisorial constraint provides an annihilating D_p-maximizing current. Positive fixed-density variational volume of its nef class would force that current's determinant-weighted measure to vanish, contradicting the positive D_p maximum. The Hopf comparison is consistent: the hyperplane class is alpha, has zero variational volume, and has a nowhere-vanishing semipositive representative. The deductions do not use BMP, a converse from P_h[u]=0, uniqueness of normalized zero-exponent potentials, whole-family convergence, singular-current products, or an equivalence between nef volume and bigness. All cited proof dependencies are internal; therefore no external-paper arXiv/web lookup was required. The supplied SHA256 for root_tail_divisorial_constraints_01 was verified.
